name: Umbral Verge

stars.name: Umbral Verge A
stars.notes: Young, brilliant white main-sequence star flooding the system with harsh ultraviolet light.

stars.name: Umbral Verge B
stars.notes: Stellar-mass black hole; its massive progenitor collapsed within the first million years, leaving a hungry shadow companion.

planets.name: Sootveil
planets.notes: Circumbinary world scoured by ancient flare events; its surface is a plain of fused black glass.

planets.name: Gravemarch
planets.notes: Canyon networks carved when the black hole last fed; tectonic groans still register on every pass.

planets.name: Pale Colossus
planets.notes: Ring system shepherded into impossible symmetry by resonance with the black hole; a navigational wonder no one dares visit.

anomalies.name: The Silent Wobble
anomalies.location: between stars A and B at the barycenter
anomalies.notes: The barycenter drifts unpredictably as accretion events shift the pair's balance; plotted orbits decay within months.

asteroid_belts.name: Glassfield Belt
asteroid_belts.notes: Fused silicate debris from an ancient flare storm; charted once and marked avoid on all standard routes.

faction_control.notes: No claim registered by any power; nav charts carry only hazard warnings where ownership papers should be.

history: An automated deep survey flagged the system as HX-2291 after detecting the black hole's accretion flicker against the white star's glare.
A salvage consortium sent one crewed vessel to assess Pale Colossus's rings; contact was lost in forty days and no second ship followed.
Today the Verge is a textbook hazard case, cited in navigator training as the reason barycenter plots require annual recertification.
description: Umbral Verge is a study in contrast: a blazing white A-class star locked in slow orbit with an eight-solar-mass black hole that drinks the light around it. Three circumbinary planets circle the uneasy pair far out in the dark, bathed in radiation and lit by a thin, shifting ring of stolen matter glowing at the hole's edge.

Nothing here invites company. No station has ever held orbit for long, no faction has filed claim, and traffic is precisely zero beyond the occasional robotic probe that never transmits twice. The system's sole export is data, gathered remotely: gravitational readings from the Silent Wobble that keep stellar dynamicists arguing in journals nobody else reads.

Rumors persist that the salvage ship Vantablack, lost during the Pale Colossus survey, still broadcasts a distress carrier on a frequency no port recognizes. The accord offices dismiss it as ghost-signal interference from the Wobble. Survey cadets are told simply this: plot wide, burn bright, and do not stop in the Verge after dark.
